terms.definition: A named boundary that groups resources and the people allowed to use them.
terms.example: Keep your staging sandboxes in a different workspace from production.

terms.definition: An isolated, disposable environment for running code and tools.
terms.example: Create a sandbox to test an app before you publish it.

terms.definition: A machine with a desktop that a person or an agent can operate.
terms.example: An agent opens a browser on a computer to complete a visual task.

terms.definition: A published application version running at a stable address.
terms.example: Publish your tested sandbox application as a deployment.

terms.definition: The top-level group that owns workspaces, membership and billing.
terms.example: Your company owns one organization with several team workspaces.

terms.definition: A person who belongs to an organization and has an assigned role.
terms.example: Invite a teammate as a viewer before granting write access.

terms.definition: A named collection of permissions that governs what someone can do.
terms.example: A read-only role can inspect a resource without changing it.

terms.definition: A human-readable name that routes traffic to an application.
terms.example: Connect app.example.com after verifying your deployment.

terms.definition: A temporary address for inspecting work before it becomes a release.
terms.example: Share the preview with a reviewer before promoting the release.

terms.definition: A numbered endpoint on a machine where a process accepts connections.
terms.example: Your development server listens on port 3000.

terms.definition: Persistent filesystem storage that can outlive the process using it.
terms.example: Mount a volume for files that must survive a restart.

terms.definition: A saved machine or filesystem state that can be restored or used to create another instance.
terms.example: Take a snapshot before installing a new dependency.

terms.definition: A service that stores and queries structured application records.
terms.example: Save customer accounts in Postgres rather than a temporary file.

terms.definition: The system that predicts and generates the agent’s next response.
terms.example: Switching the model changes reasoning, not the sandbox filesystem.

terms.definition: The program that coordinates a model, its tools and its execution loop.
terms.example: A coding harness reads files and runs commands on behalf of the model.

terms.definition: A defined action an agent can request through a controlled interface.
terms.example: The file-reading tool returns the contents of a source file.

terms.definition: The environment and software that execute a workload.
terms.example: A Python workload needs a runtime with the required interpreter and packages.

terms.definition: A packaged filesystem and configuration used to start an environment.
terms.example: Build a container image once and run the same image in staging.

terms.definition: A named configuration value available to a process when it runs.
terms.example: Keep your database connection string in server configuration instead of hard-coding it.

terms.definition: The measured resources consumed by a workload over time.
terms.example: A running machine accumulates compute usage.

terms.definition: A unit of balance that can be applied to a service’s charges.
terms.example: This reconstruction shows practice credits, not a real account balance.

terms.definition: A limit on how many resources or how much usage is allowed.
terms.example: Limit a workspace to five simultaneous sandboxes.

terms.definition: A customer boundary inside a product that serves multiple customers.
terms.example: Keep each customer’s data and permissions scoped to their tenant.

terms.definition: An explicit connection between an application and a resource it uses.
terms.example: Bind a deployment to its database configuration.

terms.definition: A product integration presented with your own name and identity.
terms.example: Show a branded preview panel inside your customer portal.
